events.label: The WTO opens
events.line: The WTO opens. Intellectual property is protected by treaty from day one.

events.label: China joins
events.line: China joins the WTO, on the assembly orbit.

events.label: Lehman
events.line: Lehman Brothers fails. The financial centre is rescued; the order holds.

events.label: Crimea
events.line: Russia takes Crimea. Washington answers with sanctions.

events.label: Brexit
events.line: Britain votes to leave the European Union. The old core starts to come apart.
events.src: Electoral Commission, referendum of 23 Jun 2016; exit day 31 Jan 2020 (S.I. 2020/74)

events.label: Section 301
events.line: Robert Lighthizer becomes Trade Representative and opens an investigation into China’s technology practices.

events.label: Appellate Body
events.line: The WTO’s Appellate Body can no longer hear appeals. Washington had blocked every new appointment since 2017.

events.label: Covid
events.line: A pandemic breaks the supply chains.

events.label: Reserves frozen
events.line: Russia’s central bank reserves are frozen. In October, the first chip export controls on China.
events.src: Joint statement 26 Feb 2022 (secondary); BIS rule 7 Oct 2022

events.label: Pax Silica
events.line: Tariffs on the whole world, then Pax Silica: the silicon curtain.
events.src: EO 14257, 2 Apr 2025; Pax Silica launched 12 Dec 2025 (State Department)

quotes.orig: China betreibt mit großem Erfolg eine aktive Industriepolitik. Das ist Ihr gutes Recht, und wir tun das auch.
quotes.text: China pursues an active industrial policy with great success. That is your good right, and we do that too.
quotes.src: Speech to the Advisory Committee of German-Chinese Business, Beijing; Bundesregierung, Bulletin 21-1

quotes.orig: Aus unserer Sicht ist es wichtig, marktverzerrende Subventionen abzubauen und dort zu einer Konsolidierung des Marktes zu kommen, wo wir Überkapazitäten sehen.
quotes.text: From our perspective, it is important to reduce market-distorting subsidies and to consolidate the market where we see overcapacities.

quotes.orig: Wer die Funktionsfähigkeit der Märkte stört, durch unfaire Subventionen, Überkapazitäten, aggressive Preissetzung oder eine künstlich unterbewertete Währung, muss mit Gegenwind rechnen.
quotes.text: Whoever disrupts the functioning of markets through unfair subsidies, overcapacities, aggressive pricing or an artificially undervalued currency must expect headwinds.
quotes.src: Speech at the Berlin Global Dialogue; Bundesregierung, Bulletin

quotes.role: staff, Article IV mission to Germany
quotes.text: Germany’s current account surplus was the world’s largest in U.S. dollar terms.
quotes.src: Concluding statement of the 2017 Article IV mission (on 2016)

quotes.text: Germany has the world’s largest current account surplus in nominal dollar terms…
quotes.src: Report to Congress, October 2018: $329bn over the four quarters to June 2018; Germany on the monitoring list

hypocrisy.source: OR1c (Gemini, 24 Nov 2026); every quote checked against the linked primary source by Claude on 24 Nov 2026

frame.line: The frame is the old order: the IMF and the World Bank (1944), the GATT (1948), the Asian Development Bank (1966) and, from 1995, the WTO. China is already inside it: the People’s Republic has held China’s seat at the IMF and the World Bank since 1980 and joined the ADB in 1986.
frame.src: IMF; World Bank; WTO; ADB (read 25 Nov 2026)

own.line: China, Russia and four Central Asian states found the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.

own.full: Swap lines of the People’s Bank of China
own.line: The People’s Bank of China signs a currency swap with the Bank of Korea, for 180 billion yuan. Hong Kong follows in January 2009.
own.src: People’s Bank of China, December 2008; HKMA, 20 Jan 2009

own.line: Brazil, Russia, India and China hold their first summit, in Yekaterinburg. South Africa joins in 2011.
own.src: President of Russia, 16 Jun 2009; BRICS India 2026

own.line: Xi Jinping proposes the Silk Road Economic Belt and the 21st-Century Maritime Silk Road: the Belt and Road.
own.src: China’s foreign ministry, “Vision and Actions”, 28 Mar 2015, on the visits of September and October 2013

own.line: The five BRICS sign the agreement on the New Development Bank in Fortaleza. It enters into force on 3 July 2015.
China switches on CIPS, its own system for cross-border payments in renminbi, on 8 October 2015.
own.src: ICBC clearing-bank notice, 8 Oct 2015; NAFMII digest of the People’s Bank’s news (the Bank’s own notice not read)

own.line: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank begins operations in Beijing with 57 founding members, Germany and the United Kingdom among them.
Five more states become full members of BRICS in January 2024, Indonesia in January 2025, as listed by the 2026 chair, India.
Twenty-nine countries sign the agreement that founds the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, in Shanghai on 16 July 2026.
own.src: China’s foreign ministry, 16 Jul 2026; State Council (Xinhua), 17 Jul 2026
